CDR_H3.rationale: CDR-H3 is the most variable loop and a dominant antigen-contact region

CDR_L3.rationale: CDR-L3 frequently contributes to antigen binding

CDR_H2.rationale: CDR-H2 can modulate binding orientation and affinity

CDR_L1.rationale: CDR-L1 can participate in antigen contacts

CDR_regions.allowed_substitutions: All 20 standard amino acids considered; preference for physicochemically similar substitutions
avoid: Proline at internal loop positions unless structurally justified
Any change to conserved framework residues

soft_constraints: Avoid deamidation-prone motifs (e.g., NG, NS, DG) in exposed loops
Maintain overall net charge within approximately ±2 of the starting sequence
Limit contiguous hydrophobic stretches to reduce aggregation risk
Preserve known disulfide bonds and structural anchors

antigen_preferences.guidance: No antigen hotspots, glycans, forbidden positions, or bound residue information were provided. Antigen preferences are therefore weak and sequence-level only; do not assume specific epitope residues.
